human_tolerance.notes: Familiar in settled areas near food, scavenging from bird feeders, vegetable gardens, compost piles, garbage cans and pet food; because it is slow and nocturnal and is drawn to roadside carrion, it is more likely than other animals in its range to become roadkill.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: The breeding season can begin as early as December and continue through October, with most young born between February and June; a female may have one to three litters a year, and the male attracts the female with clicking sounds.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Gestation lasts 11-13 days and the average litter is 8-9 infants, though over 20 may be born. The young are born extremely undeveloped, latch onto one of 13 teats, stay latched for two months and in the pouch for two and a half months, then ride on the mother's back, learning survival skills. Only one in ten offspring survive to reproductive adulthood.

phases.name: dormancy
phases.note: Not true hibernation: the opossum does not hibernate but reduces its activity in winter, and may not leave its den for several days if the temperature falls below about -7 to -4 C.

vocalizations.description: An open-mouth hiss given when frightened, when the animal also bares its 50 teeth, snaps its jaw, drools and stands its fur on end to look bigger. The hiss is widely mistaken for rabid behaviour, though opossums are naturally resistant to rabies.
Clicking sounds made with the mouth, used by the male to attract the female during the mating season.

range.note: Found from southern Canada to northern Costa Rica, the northernmost marsupial in the world, and expanding its range northward and northwestward; it was intentionally introduced into the West during the Great Depression and now occupies much of the Pacific coast, which is not recorded as an introduction here because the country is already listed as native.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Wikipedia documents the pacing gait (limbs on one side moved together, then the other) and a faster running pattern from its track measurements; a short trot is the mapping of that run. Climbing is not described in the sections used here and is included as authored judgement from a lightly built, grasping-handed marsupial.

traits.metamorphosis.note: Although it is a marsupial, Wikipedia describes newborn opossums as born extremely undeveloped and latching onto a teat, with no larval or pupal stage.

traits.nest_type.note: Authored judgement: the article describes a den that the female may not leave for several days in cold weather but does not describe the den itself in the sections used here; Cavity is the nearest matching value for a den in a hollow or enclosed site rather than a burrow it digs.

traits.perching.note: Set to false: the species walks and runs on the ground and is described as a ground-going nocturnal animal that takes to the air only in the sense of not hibernate; it is not a perching animal.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's weights for males (2.1-2.8 kg) and females (1.9-2.1 kg): the midpoints are 2.45 and 2.0 kg, and their mean is about 2.35 kg.

traits.length_m.note: The schema wants nose to tail tip. Wikipedia gives 33-55 cm from snout to the base of the tail plus a tail of 25-54 cm; the midpoints of each (44 cm and 39.5 cm) are added to give 0.835 m, rounded to 0.84 m.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Wikipedia describes the animal as 'about the size of a domestic cat' and gives no measurement. 0.25 m is the shoulder height of an adult domestic cat, used here as the stated reference animal; no open source used here gives the opossum's own shoulder height.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'The Virginia opossum has a maximal lifespan in the wild of only about two years', and about four years even in captivity.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia describes an omnivore taking a wide range of plant food and, among animal foods, small invertebrates, carrion, eggs, fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and small mammals, with insects (grasshoppers, crickets and beetles) making up the bulk of the animal foods. No open source gives percentages, so the 35/20/20/15/10 split across invertebrate, fruit, carrion, small vertebrate and browse is authored judgement within the described bounds.

traits.social.note: 'a solitary nocturnal animal'; the group size allows two for a female travelling with young on her back.

traits.activity_pattern.note: 'a solitary nocturnal animal', and Wikipedia repeatedly describes its slow nocturnal nature and night foraging.

traits.defense.note: When threatened an opossum either flees or takes a stand by baring 50 teeth, snapping its jaw, hissing, drooling and standing its fur on end, and it is well known to feign death or 'play possum'. Freeze is the mapping of the thanatosis response, which is the one the schema records.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: very low wariness - it forages in daylight in some circumstances, scavenges from pet food and compost in settled areas, and famously 'plays possum' rather than bolting.

habitat.use.note: The strong ground share follows Wikipedia's account of a slow ground-going animal that takes to the air only as a last resort; the small arboreal share is authored judgement from the grasping hands and prehensile tail of an arboreal marsupial.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored judgement, following traits.nest_type: the den is an enclosed site rather than a burrow the animal digs.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet. The compost entry follows Wikipedia's record of urban opossums scavenging from compost piles, garbage cans, bird feeders and vegetable gardens, recorded here as a landscape resource rather than a food type.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia describes opossums as familiar to many North Americans because they inhabit settled areas near food sources such as trash cans, pet food, compost piles, gardens and houses, and names the scavenging list in the Diet section; road mortality follows the same passage.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'It does not hibernate but reduces its activity during the winter', so ActiveYearRound with a dormant winter phase is the mapping.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding-season dates, litter size, gestation, pouch and latching durations and the survival figure are from the Reproduction section; the winter denning figure is from the hibernation paragraph. The month bounds of the young phase are authored judgement, as the article gives only the February-June peak.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Wikipedia describes about two months latched and two and a half months in the pouch, then learning survival skills on the mother's back, but gives no total weaning age; 120 days and the scale are authored judgement.

vocalizations.note: The open-mouth hiss with bared teeth, jaw-snapping and raised fur, and the male's mating click, are both described in Wikipedia's Behaviour and Reproduction sections; the cooldowns and the night time window are authored judgement.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia's description of a cat-sized animal with coarse greyish-white fur, a white face and a dark muzzle, and a long sparsely furred tail; the palette and proportions are authored judgement to render the pointed snout and long bare tail, and the tail_fur part thins the tail along its length.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared ground-forager program. The sun band is left at the program's daytime default because the species is nocturnal, so it rests in its den by day; flee_gait is a short trot and food_tag is 'invertebrate' because insects are the bulk of its animal prey. All radii are judgement, set short for a slow, human-tolerant animal.
